text:
Maya: Heads up — after enabling the FP8 runtime path on H100/L40S canaries, we're seeing intermittent p99 spikes and tail latency anomalies. Repro rate ~3% of requests, mostly long-context (>=2k tokens).
Raj: Any logs or traces to start with?
Maya: Pasting a trimmed canary trace (timestamps normalized):
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:05Z] kernel_switch: from=fp8_te to=int8_slowpath reason=fallback_sync
[2026-03-17T14:12:05Z] queue_fence_wait=187ms kv_cache_evictions=12
[2026-03-17T14:12:05Z] microbatch_enqueue_ms=42 kernel_launch_ms=210
```
Simon: That queue_fence_wait is the smoking gun — async kernel handoff plus a synchronous fallback is stalling the thread. Looks like the TE async submit isn't compatible with the fallback slowpath.
Kai: We're also seeing elevated kv_cache_evictions correlated with the same requests; cache churn could be triggering larger tiling/activation footprints which then trips the TE thresholds.
Maya: Local repro command (minimal):
```
./bench_infer --model rwd-galaxy-7b --precision fp8 --batch 4 --seq 4096 --burst 8 --profile=kv,kernels
```
Maya: If I set TRANSFORMER_ENGINE_ASYNC=0 the p99 stabilizes but sustained throughput drops ~8%. So async helps but it's unsafe with the current fallback interactions.
Raj: So two levers: keep async and fix the fallback interaction, or disable async during rollout. Any quick mitigations?
Simon: From the profiler, fallback is triggered by tiling mismatch when activation range > TE calibration threshold — an FP8 calibration edge-case. Kernel selector currently prefers TE when available, then falls back to int8_slowpath without coordinating the submit semantics. We need a coordinated selector that considers async semantics.
Maya: Telemetry snapshot for affected canary: kernel_switches_per_min=85, fence_wait_p99=160ms, kv_eviction_rate=0.09. Baseline (non-FP8) pools: kernel_switches_per_min=2, fence_wait_p99=8ms.
perf-bot: Canary canary-mlp-02: automatic rollback executed (reason=tail_latency_regression) :warning:
Maya: Quick patch I pushed to the canary branch: 1) per-model kernel_safelist env (RWD_KERNEL_SAFELIST), 2) auto-disable async handoff for sequences > 2048, 3) bumped TE compile timeout and retry window.
Kai: Microbatch enqueue jitter might be amplifying this — batching heuristics add variance to microbatch sizes which changes tiling decisions mid-flight. Could increase microbatch debounce or add a minimum batch occupancy to smooth behavior.
Raj: Can we add observability fields: fence_wait_reason and kernel_fallback_reason in the per-request telemetry? Filtering by those will make debugging much faster.
Simon: Also propose a temporary runtime heuristic: if kv_cache_evictions > 5 in the last 10s for a worker, prefer int8_safepath for new requests to avoid oscillation between FP8_TE and fallback. This reduces kernel_switch churn.
Maya: I'm running a full microbench across H100/L40S and will upload per-request kernel decisions + KV events to /tmp/fp8-probe-trace.jsonl and share. Expect ~10k requests in ~30min.
Kai: Opening INF-4823 to track follow-ups and rollout gating, assigning to eng-runtime. Will add a checklist: telemetry fields, kernel selector patch, conservative rollout flag.
Maya: Thanks — will post the trace when complete. If anyone sees similar spikes in other pools, ping here and attach the probe trace. :thumbsup:
